subject: Support SLA: staggered uptime bands, credit ceilings & emergency patch windows
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: David Mills <david.mills@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Support SLA: staggered uptime bands, credit ceilings & emergency patch windows

David —

Thanks for sending your procurement team's markup. We walked through Brightline's redlines and I wanted to put a short, concrete counterproposal on the table so legal and procurement can evaluate tradeoffs quickly. High-level items below: 

- Uptime bands: we propose a 3-tier availability schedule (99.99%, 99.95%, 99.9%) tied to prorated credit tiers. This gives you stronger protection at higher availability while keeping costs predictable.
- Credit ceilings: Redwood proposes a monthly cap equal to 50% of the monthly recurring charge (MRC) for service credit payouts. We understand Brightline asked for no cap; this cap protects both sides from outsized, cascading credits in rare multi-region incidents.
- Response SLAs: P1 response within 30 minutes, P2 within 2 hours, P3 within 8 business hours (definitions included in the attached checklist).
- Maintenance windows: standard maintenance will be scheduled during a weekly 4-hour window with a 72-hour notice; emergency patching will be allowed with a 4-hour advance notice where possible and a 2-hour SLA for urgent patches during P1 incidents.

Attachments: redline-summary.pdf (high-level), uptime-evidence-checklist.xlsx (what we can share for evidence requests). I flagged three points for legal attention which will speed a final order form: credit cap language, emergency patch carveouts, and evidence request cadence.

Next steps: if Brightline is open to the 50% cap and the proposed maintenance cadence, we can route an MSA addendum for signatures and schedule a 30-minute legal sync.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redline-summary.pdf, uptime-evidence-checklist.xlsx

From: David Mills <david.mills@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support SLA: staggered uptime bands, credit ceilings & emergency patch windows

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few quick reactions from procurement and our legal counsel: 

- The uptime bands look fine, but Brightline is concerned the 50% monthly cap is too high. Our preference is a 25% cap or no cap for high-availability services. Can you explain how Redwood landed on 50%?
- Emergency patch language: our security team is worried about a broad carveout that allows urgent patches without a blackout window. They'd like stricter criteria for what qualifies as "emergency" and a mandatory post-patch audit log.
- Evidence requests: procurement asked for an example of the audit packet we would provide for a credit claim.

I've attached our initial redlines for legal (Brightline_redlines_v1.docx). Can we get a track-changes summary + a call early this week? Our procurement lead is out Wednesday, so Tuesday afternoon or Thursday morning PT works.

Thanks —
David Mills
VP, Procurement — Brightline Health
David.Mills@brightlinehealth.com | +1 206-555-8222

Attachments: Brightline_redlines_v1.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support SLA: staggered uptime bands, credit ceilings & emergency patch windows

Team —

I reviewed Brightline's doc and Kimberly's counters. A few legal notes (high level) to prepare for the sync: 

1) Credit cap rationale: the 50% cap is standard for Redwood's order forms; it's defensible because it prevents runaway liabilities and is tied to the MRC (not total contract value). If Brightline insists on 25% we should request a shorter credit lookback window (30 days) and explicit mitigation obligations from Brightline (e.g., alternate region failover steps).

2) Emergency patch carveout: tighten the definition — limit to "vulnerability with CVSS >= 9.0 or confirmed material data-exfiltration risk" and require a post-implementation report within 48 hours (audit artifact: patch diff, deployment tag, and system logs). That should assuage their security team while preserving our ability to act quickly.

3) Evidence packet: uptime-evidence-checklist.xlsx is a good start. Add a hash-signed log export, aggregated KV cache metrics, and per-token latency histogram for the incident window. Per legal, we should also offer a short SOC-2 extract where applicable.

Proposed attendees for the Tuesday call: Kimberly (sales), Jonas (VP Sales), Marissa (Customer Success), David (procurement), Brightline legal, and Brightline security. Jonas — can you take the Tuesday 2:30pm PT slot if David confirms?

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Mills <david.mills@brightlinehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support SLA: staggered uptime bands, credit ceilings & emergency patch windows

David —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing your redlines. Putting a pragmatic compromise forward from our side to unblock procurement: 

- Credit ceiling compromise: cap at the lesser of 50% of MRC or $250k per month for the first 12 months of the contract. This limits exposure while giving Brightline stronger protection early post-deployment.
- Emergency patch guardrails: adopt Laura's tightened definition. Add a mandatory 24-hour notice where operationally possible and a post-patch audit within 48 hours. For true zero-day infrared events we keep the 2-hour patching carveout.
- Evidence packet: we'll produce the redline summary + an example evidence packet (redline-summary.pdf + uptime-evidence-checklist.xlsx). If Brightline wants a deeper review, we can offer a one-time SOC-2 extract for procurement review under NDA.

If procurement can accept the $250k cap for year one, we can move to DocuSign for the order form and lock in onboarding dates. Proposed legal sync Tuesday 2:30pm PT.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
